key_insight: Averaging thermodynamic dislocation theory over grain orientations turns macroscopic plasticity into an associated J2 flow model, with hardening emerging from dislocation kinetics rather than curve fitting.
engineering_relevance: This provides a single physics-based constitutive law that can predict tension, compression, and torsion of copper across wide temperatures and strain rates, enabling more reliable solid-mechanics simulations.
method: Assume equal-probability grain orientations and compute root-mean-square averages of resolved shear stress/strain over slip systems.
Use exact isotropic orientation identities to link mean resolved shear stress to von Mises stress and plastic flow direction to the stress deviator.
Write dislocation-density and effective-temperature evolution as time rates so arbitrary loading paths and torsion can be modeled directly.
evidence_signal: A single parameter set matches 142 data points for copper across tension, compression, and torsion from room temperature to 1173 K and 10 to 2300 s^-1, within about 6% rms.
watch_item: The predicted torsion response depends on the assumed initial dislocation state, so specimen history and preprocessing must be controlled carefully.
paper_title: Averaging in thermodynamic dislocation theory: general macroscopically uniform stress and strain states
